## Design

### 2026-10-11 – ![Downstream Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/32e7de20d9229e0968c1e5609ce636575d9d769453a25f858d37fec3ee8fd2ee.png)

**3h**

![Downstream Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/32e7de20d9229e0968c1e5609ce636575d9d769453a25f858d37fec3ee8fd2ee.png)
This was my first time ever designing a PCB, so it was a very slow process at first. I learned the basics from a few tutorials and began working on it with basically no plan. First, I completed the upstream (It says downstream, but I mixed the two up), which is basically the male USB that plugs into a device.

![BugFixing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/cf836de890566e4be4bf2a70e09fded6d298af6f34ed44a0a374a3980dd0fe95.png)
I then encountered a couple of errors, which I had to do even more research on in order to fix. It was actually quite simple, though, and I managed to fix all of those up.

![FullSchematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/6c4226de193bc20a4d5f102ce1ccda94445501288a0da9280f9f8fb6c37dcc1c.png)
I proceeded to work on the rest of the schematic- the downstream parts where you can plug in two USB-A and 2 USB C devices. This was the harder part of the project, but again, by following the tutorial on Hack Club and with the help of others, I finished the whole thing.

### 2026-10-11 – ![Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/fe5ba12d1c41bc6a5515dfc6664d3d350b564b3afcc3bfe40a8d2885be269648.png)

**6h**

![Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/fe5ba12d1c41bc6a5515dfc6664d3d350b564b3afcc3bfe40a8d2885be269648.png)
In order to turn the schematic into a PCB design, I needed to find physical components that correspond to the design that I could use. Again, I don't know anything about components so I looked the parts up and decided to go with the simplest ones I could find that worked for me.

![RawPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/b90e06fc6fed10e27c1ebb991d5cdda03deadabbdb00f1ece3e75cb4a6ebc43f.png)
Then I imported the schematic into the PCB design software, which is what the picture above shows. Turns out, this would take even longer than the schematic since the connections can't overlap each other, which I didn't know.

![Capacitators and Resistors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/9c9d0398ec6e8b7afec45f3f6d4569300d18d298e2904e4729daa015b60acb59.png)
I started off with something simple: the resistors and capacitors that had few connections. I tweaked them around for a bit, and this is when I realized that the connections can't overlap.

![Rearranged PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/6e91f0791f4c9701cab7a39394cdb053fe7e02958758c47dff28350ca20e08b4.png)
So, I completely started over and began wiring everything from scratch. This proved to be much more time-consuming and difficult. I kept having to change things up and tweak things because the wires would block each other and get in the way. This was definitely the longest part of the project.

![Errors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5de2e7b33969534fdd18700f1dbbfebd46f85316bab3a8da780baef1df3c62cb.png)
Just when I thought I was done, I was hit with 25 error messages. Honestly, I wanted to quit because I'd already been working on it for so long, but I powered through and fixed all of them one by one, which took forever. It was anything from unconnected items to hole clearance violations.

![FinalPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/dc13f089319dda2284e4260c47972a1655bba21f11a5fbc305b59c3b3bbfb2b5.png)
Finally, once that was done, I added a back copper layer that connected all of my ground pins and made the final finishing touches.
